newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies bid to delay second-hand smoking suit.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies bid to delay second-hand smoking suit.

text.p: A Florida judge has denied a tobacco industry request to postpone a trial in a lawsuit filed by non-smoking flight attendants who claim they were sickened by second-hand smoke aboard passenger jets.
Dade County Judge Robert Kaye, in a ruling signed on Friday and issued to lawyers over the weekend, denied a motion for delay made by tobacco industry lawyers at a hearing last week.
Kaye said in the ruling that the lawyers for the flight attendants had agreed to reduce the number of witnesses and papers they would present at the trial, which is scheduled to begin on June 2.

Tobacco industry lawyers told Kaye last week that they needed at least another month to question witnesses and go through documents to be adequately prepared for trial. Kaye in April turned down another industry request for a delay.
While the lawsuit does not seek a specific amount in damages, the trial in the class-action suit is expected to be closely watched.

In the suit, Miami lawyers Stanley and Susan Rosenblatt are claiming damages on behalf of an estimated 60,000 non-smoking flight attendants suffering from lung diseases and other ailments allegedly caused by second-hand smoke on U.S. passenger jets.
